title: The heads of the biggest AI labs want to agree among themselves on when everyone should slow down. @TheEconomist's piece on that push ends with Covenant-72B, the model we finished training in March on GPUs contributed over the internet, as a reason such agreements may be hard to enforce. What the piece doesn't say is that once training no longer requires one giant, tightly connected cluster, the power to build new models no longer has to sit with a few companies. Globally distributed training and open models are essential tools for keeping that power from concentrating in the frontier labs.
